clue.text: Cheats on white-haired father in braces

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other, the father placed within the braces

parts.note: a brace is a pair, so braces are twos
Father Time is traditionally pictured as an old man with white hair

explanation.surface: Someone is unfaithful to an elderly father who wears braces to hold his trousers up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'braces' looks like trouser straps, but a brace is a pair (a brace of pheasants), so braces are TWOS.
explanation.definitionFit: To two-time a partner is to be unfaithful by secretly seeing someone else as well.

clue.text: Bill was first put up for debate

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab
to have led is to have been first

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill was the first proposed for discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage to table a motion is to propose it for discussion; in American usage it means to shelve it.
explanation.definitionFit: To table a matter in Britain is to submit it for discussion at a meeting.

clue.text: Nothing put Nelly off like millionaires

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

indicators.note: off means wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rich crowd were not put off by Nelly at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Opulently means richly and lavishly, the way millionaires live.

clue.text: Language from one book rejected by Afghan movement

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: rejected by says the movement throws out the book

parts.note: the Taliban is an Afghan Islamist movement

explanation.surface: A tongue taken from a single book banned by the Taliban.
explanation.definitionFit: Italian is the language spoken in Italy.

clue.text: Artist makes point to Fleet Street

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point
RN, the Royal Navy, is the British fleet

explanation.surface: A painter makes a point to the national newspapers of Fleet Street.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleet Street, London's old newspaper district, is split in two here.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Surrealist and Dada painter, so an example of an artist.

clue.text: Private chasing women's a success

parts.note: private thoughts are inner ones, kept to oneself

explanation.surface: A private soldier pursues women and thinks it a triumph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' places INNER after W; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A winner is something or someone that turns out to be a hit or triumph.

clue.text: One's secular, retaining mark of faith

parts.note: I is one, with 's giving S

indicators.note: retaining means keeping something inside, so the secular word holds the mark

parts.note: laic means lay, not of the clergy, secular
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Someone who is secular nonetheless keeps a sign of religious belief.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits secular against faith, though 'secular' only supplies LAIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Islamic describes things belonging to Islam, so it is an adjective meaning of a particular faith.

clue.text: Vegetables spotted covering top of pot up

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, says the letters are read from bottom to top
covering means wrapping around, so the spotted word encloses the letter

parts.note: spotted means seen

indicators.note: top of picks the first letter of the word pot

explanation.surface: Vegetables were noticed spilling over the top of a cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEN around P makes SPEEN, which 'up' turns to read bottom to top. NEEPS is the Scottish word for turnips or swedes.
explanation.definitionFit: Neeps are turnips or swedes, a Scots word for root vegetables.

clue.text: One or two girls got up to go to altar — one runs away

parts.note: rose means got up

indicators.note: away says one letter is taken out of the wedding word

parts.note: to go to the altar is to marry
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A couple of girls rose to go to the altar, but one bolted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one runs away' removes one of the two Rs in MARRY. The answer is one girl's name, or two joined: Rose and Mary.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is a girl's name, and it splits into the two names Rose and Mary.

clue.text: Force out to criticise freemasons, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly says the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: to diss is to criticise, and a lodge is a freemasons' branch

explanation.surface: Someone is said to attack the freemasons.
explanation.definitionFit: To dislodge something is to knock or force it out of position.

clue.text: USA gave a billion for reconstructing plants

indicators.note: reconstructing means building again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: America donated a huge sum to rebuild industrial plants.
explanation.walkthrough: All fifteen letters of USA GAVE A BILLION are rearranged; 'plants' reads as factories in the surface but means flowering climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are tropical climbing shrubs with bright papery bracts, so they are examples of plants.

clue.text: Stranger grabbing supporter is bemoaning linesman

indicators.note: grabbing means holding something within, so the stranger's letters surround the rest

parts.note: ET, the extraterrestrial, is the ultimate stranger
a leg supports a table or a body
taken as written

explanation.surface: A newcomer seizing a fan is then a sulky line judge at a football match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'linesman' suggests a match official but here means a writer of lines of verse, one who laments in them.
explanation.definitionFit: An elegist writes elegies, mournful poems lamenting the dead, so is a poet who bemoans in verse.

clue.text: House sitter in America placed in chimney one lot of money

indicators.note: placed in signals that the American piece goes inside the chimney

parts.note: LUM is a Scottish and northern English word for a chimney

indicators.note: in puts the House sitter within the country's abbreviation

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States
an MP sits in the House of Commons

explanation.surface: Someone minding a house in America has stashed a single payment up the chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House sitter' looks like someone minding a home but is a Member of Parliament (MP), who sits in the House.
explanation.definitionFit: A lump sum is a single payment made all at once rather than in instalments.

clue.text: Departure point one associated with Hardy's Heath

parts.note: Stan Laurel was partnered with Oliver Hardy, so one associated with Hardy's is Stan's
Edward Heath, British Prime Minister 1970-74, was known as Ted

explanation.surface: A point of departure linked to the heath in Thomas Hardy's novels.
explanation.walkthrough: Hardy and Heath suggest Thomas Hardy's Egdon Heath, but Hardy is Oliver Hardy of Laurel and Hardy and Heath is the politician Ted Heath. STANSTED is a London airport.
explanation.definitionFit: Stansted is one of London's airports, a place from which flights leave.

clue.text: Vehicle in short supply youth club's leaders got for grand

indicators.note: got for says one thing is obtained in exchange for another, a swap

parts.note: a trickle is a meagre flow, a short supply
K stands for a thousand, a grand

indicators.note: leaders picks the first letters of youth and club's

explanation.surface: A vehicle is scarce, but the youth club's bosses got one for a thousand pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: In TRICKLE, K (grand) is swapped for YC.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricycle is a three-wheeled cycle, a kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Shrink's business with leading lady

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the Queen, is the country's leading lady

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist's practice teams up with the star actress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrink' reads as a psychiatrist, but it is the verb, to recoil in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: To cower is to cringe or recoil in fear, a synonym for shrinking back.

clue.text: Promise forger he'd be good at coining?

parts.note: to give one's word is to promise
a smith forges metal

explanation.surface: A counterfeiter vows he could make convincing coins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forger' and 'coining' suggest counterfeit money, but a smith forges metal and the coining is of new words.
explanation.definitionFit: A wordsmith is a skilled user of words, the kind of person who coins new terms.

clue.text: Last in at such a late hour?

definitions.meaning: in cricket the number eleven batsman is the last to go in
doing something at the ... hour means at the last moment

explanation.definitionFit: The eleventh batsman bats last, and the eleventh hour is a byword for the last minute.

clue.text: Produce eggs bound for city store

parts.note: hens lay eggs
one goes up to a city, especially London, so heading townwards is up

explanation.surface: A farmer produces eggs to sell at a shop in town.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go 'up' to London or a university city.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay up goods is to put them aside and keep them for future use.

clue.text: Radio show makes piano tune fashionable

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
to hone is to fine-tune or sharpen
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A radio programme plays a fashionable piano tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tune' looks like a melody but is a verb, to refine.
explanation.definitionFit: A phone-in is a radio programme in which listeners call to speak on air.

clue.text: Amateur theatre returning one then comes across

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: comes across means spanning or enclosing, so this piece goes around the theatre

parts.note: next means then, afterwards

indicators.note: returning means the theatre word is read backwards

parts.note: REP is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: An amateur drama group returns and someone then arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpert means lacking skill, which is how an amateur or unskilled person performs.

clue.text: Instruction in making Jersey EU territory, peripherally

parts.note: purl one, PURL I, is a knitting instruction for a jersey (a jumper)
taken as written

explanation.surface: Knitting directions for a Jersey jumper border on European Union land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' with a capital suggests the Channel Island, but it is a knitted jersey, or jumper; 'purl one' is a knitting pattern instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Purlieus are the outskirts or surrounding area of a place, territory at its edges.

clue.text: Prize drugs are in plentiful supply

parts.note: E is ecstasy, so Es are drugs
to teem is to be abundant

explanation.surface: Banned substances are plentiful among prizewinners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prize' reads as a reward but is the verb, to value highly.
explanation.definitionFit: To esteem something is to value it highly, the verb sense of prize.

clue.text: Dry rot civilian conceals when turning over old naval vessel

indicators.note: turning over says the concealed letters are read from right to left
conceals says the answer sits within the run of these clue words

explanation.surface: A civilian hides dry rot found while overhauling a former warship.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading DRY ROT CIV backwards gives the run.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Victory was Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar and is preserved as an old warship.

clue.text: Sadistic clue setter finally changed …

indicators.note: changed signals these letters are rearranged into a new order
finally picks the last letter of setter

explanation.surface: A cruel compiler finally altered a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruel describes someone who enjoys causing pain, which is what sadistic means.

clue.text: Lever going in unserviceable lifts

indicators.note: going in signals that the lever goes inside the unserviceable abbreviation

parts.note: to prise is to lever something open

explanation.surface: A crowbar is jammed into elevators that are out of order.
explanation.definitionFit: Uprises is an old verb meaning rises up, and lifts as a verb means rises, a synonym.

clue.text: … that's resolved a sore point

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: that refers back to the previous clue's answer, the word meaning sadistic

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a painful issue is settled.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to 24-down: 'that' is its answer, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An ulcer is an open sore, so a painful spot on the body.

clue.text: On cue, unveil lies to damage chef's style

indicators.note: to damage something is to wreck it, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: On a signal, someone reveals untruths meant to harm a cook's reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouvelle cuisine is a style of cooking with light dishes and artful presentation, a chef's approach.

clue.text: State capital providing railway through Orpington area?

indicators.note: through means running inside, so the railway goes within the hen

parts.note: the Orpington is a breed of hen
EL is the elevated railway, especially Chicago's

explanation.surface: A capital city on a railway line running through the Orpington district.
explanation.walkthrough: Orpington is a London suburb, but also a breed of chicken, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Helena is the capital of the US state of Montana.

clue.text: Carriage, second class, not even coming before noon

parts.note: B is the grade below A, second class
a rough surface is not even
AM, ante meridiem, means before noon

explanation.surface: A second-class railway coach runs on bumpy track in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A brougham is a light, four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage named after Lord Brougham.
